caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1059 of 2002
lawyer:
Mr. Abdur Razzaq, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record ----- for the petitioner
Mr. ASM Khalequezaman, Advocate-on-Record ----- for Respondent No. 1
Mr. Tufailur Rahman, Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Ahmed Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No. 2. 
Respondent Nos. 3-11----- Not represented
parties:
Md. Mozibur Rahman and others
Vs.
Md. Shamsul Alam Miah & ors
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J:- Added respondent-petitioners seek leave to appeal against the impugned judgment and order dated 3rd April 2002 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3622 of 2000 making the rule absolute-in-part. 

 2. The respondent No. 1 as the writ petitioner filed the writ petition challenging the Order No. 1092 dated 21.06.2000 issued under the signature of the Secretary, Dhaka City Corporation for giving current charge of 14 posts of Deputy Taxation Officers of the Corporation to the respondent Nos. 5-18 to the writ petition. That writ petitioner filed an application for promotion to the post of Deputy Taxation Officer before the Chief Executive Officer, Dhaka City Corporation, Nagar Bhaban, Dhaka according to the provisions of Dhaka City Corporation Employees Service Rules, 1989 which has been framed under Section 157 of the Dhaka Municipal Corporation Ordinance 1983 (XL of 1983). That without complying with the legal provisions of the Municipal Corporation Rules by the writ respondent No. 2, 14 persons have been promoted to the post of Deputy Taxation of who are junior to writ petitioner. Besides, the said 14 persons being not eligible to the said posts on 28.06.2000 the writ petitioner filed an application before the Chief Executive Officer of Dhaka City Corporation challenging their promotion. It was further stated in the writ petition that by Order No. 669 dated 5.5.1986 the writ petitioner and others have been selected for different posts upon their agreeing to forego their service seniority, and accordingly after the interviews held on 24.4.1986 and 26.4.1986 and 26.4.1986, they have been posted to the post of UDA-cum-Accountant Superintending Engineer's Office, Circle-1 upon certain terms and conditions. That the promotion of the employees of Dhaka City Corporation is governed by the Rules 15,16 and the Schedule to the Dhaka Municipal Corporation Employees Service Rules, 1989 which have been framed under the Dhaka Municipal Ordinance, 1983 (XI of 1983). That without complying with the aforesaid Rules the writ-respondent no. 2 by his order No. 1092 dated 21.6.2000 most illegally promoted the 14 persons (which in-10 dudes the writ-petitioners herein) to the post of Deputy Taxation Officer (DTO) by superseding the writ-petitioner and others. Moreover, under the Rules the said 14 persons were not eligible to promotion. In the premises the writ petitioner submitted that the impugned order of promotion without considering his case was unlawful, arbitrary and without jurisdiction in as much as the same is contrary to Rule 15, 16 and Schedule to the Municipal Corporation Employees Service Rules, 1983 and therefore violative of Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution. Finally it was stated in the writ petition that the writ-petitioner has moved the High Court Division to redress a public wrong or public injury, and although the writ-petitioner may not have any personal interest in the matter he must be deemed to have 'sufficient interest' and therefore has locus standi to move this application under Article 102 of the Constitution, not-withstanding the fact that there is a provision for appeal under Rule 48 of Dhaka Municipal Corporation Employees Service Rules, 1988, as the same is not an equally efficacious remedy. 

 3. The writ-respondent Nos. 2 to 4 contested the rule contending, inter alia, that in a meeting of the selection committee No. 1 of the Dhaka City Corporation held on 20.07.1999 the question of promotion to the post of Deputy Taxation Officer (hereinafter DTO), confirmation of service and certain cases of absorption were considered. The committee, on examining the working papers and upon clue deliberations found that all the listed persons were Class-III employees and working in the feeder posts of Deputy Taxation Officer as per schedule of Dhaka City Corporation Employees Service Rules 1989. According to the previous pay scale of 1997 (Tk. 3,400-6625) the post of Deputy Taxation Officer ranked as Class-11 and therefore there was no illegality in giving promotion to the post of D.T.O from the feeder post of Class-III. The pay scale to the post of Deputy Taxation Officer has been enhanced to a higher scale of Tk. 4300-7740/- and as a result of which the post of DTO has been upgraded to Class-I status. In that view of the matter the committee did not consider it wise to till up Class-I post from the Class-III feeder post and as such the opinion of the Ministry of L.G.R.D. and Co-Operatives was sought. On the other hand, the Chief Revenue Officer informed the Committee that due to the shortage of Deputy Taxation Officer the works of Revenue Department were being hampered. After detailed discussion the committee decided to give temporary charge to the posts of Deputy Taxation Officer from amongst the persons working in Class-Ill the feeder posts. This was done in accordance with the schedule of Dhaka City Corporation Employees Service Rules 1989, and as per list placed before the selection committee on the basis of the seniority, satisfactory service records, efficiency etc. of the feeder post employees. In the meantime proposals for including some other posts such as Section Assistant/Head Assistant Accountant, Assistant Accountant, Senior Superior (Revenue), UDA-cum-Accountant, Stenographer, Personal Assistant, Steno-Typist, Market Supervisor, to the feeder posts of Deputy Taxation Officer have been sent to the Ministry of LGRD and Cooperative and a decision to that effect from the Ministry was still awaiting. Therefore, for the better interest of administration of Revenue Department it was decided to give temporary charges to the post of Deputy Taxation Officer from among the persons who are working in the feeder posts and also from among the graduate persons who were working in the proposed feeder posts of Deputy taxation Officer and possesses the necessary experience in the Revenue Department. Accordingly 14 (fourteen) persons had been given temporary charge of the posts of Deputy Taxation Officer Vide Dhaka City Corporation Office Order No. 1092 dated 21.06. 2000. The writ petitioner has got no work ex-presence in the Revenue Department and as such he was not considered eligible to hold temporary charge as Deputy Taxation Officer. In the body of the impugned order it was stated that temporary charge given to the persons would not be treated as promotion and the persons so promoted on temporary basis cannot claim permanent promotion as of right The impugned order No. 1092 dated 20.07.99 issued by the Dhaka City Corporation was not an order of promotion, but merely an order giving temporary charge to the respondents. Hence, the petitioner had nothing to be aggrieved of. 

 4. The added respondent petitioners contested the rule stating, inter alia, that a meeting of the selection committee No. 1 of the Dhaka City Corporation was held on 20.07.99. In the meeting several promotional cases including promotion to the post of Deputy Taxation Officer (hereinafter DTO), confirmation of service and some absorption cases were placed before the committee for consideration. The committee on examining the working papers found that all the listed persons are Class III employees and they are working in the feeder posts of Deputy Taxation Officer as per schedule of DCC Service Rules 1989. Since as per the previous pay scale/1997 (Tk. 3,400-6625) the post of Deputy Taxation Officer was Class-II status. Very recently the pay scale of the post of Deputy Taxation Officer has been enhanced to a higher scale of Tk. 4300-7740/- as a result the post of DTO has become Class-I post. As it was not just to fill up the Class-1 post by the feeder post holding Class-III employees the committee opined to elevate the post of marketing Supervisor to Class-II post. Accordingly, a letter has already been written to the Ministry of L.G.R.D. and Co-operatives for this purpose. Moreover, since due to the shortage of Deputy Taxation Officer in Dhaka City Corporation the works of Revenue Department were being hampered the committee took a decision to give temporary charge to the posts of Deputy Taxation Officer from amongst the persons working to the post of Marketing Supervisor and Assistant Social Welfare Officer. 

 5. That in the meantime proposals for including some other posts such as Section Assistant/Head Assistant Accountant, Assistant Accountant, Senior Superior, (Revenue), U.D.A. Cum-Accountant, Stenographer, Personal Assistant, Steno-Typist, Market Supervisor, to the feeder posts of Deputy Taxation Officer have been sent to the Ministry of L.G.R.D. and Co-operation and decision to this effect still awaiting. Therefore, for the better interest of administration Revenue Department, it has been decided to give temporary charges to the post of Deputy Taxation Officer from amongst the persons who are working in the feeder posts of Deputy Taxation Officer and also from amongst the graduate persons who are working in the proposed feeder posts of Deputy Taxation Officers and possesses the experience in the work of Revenue Department. Accordingly 14(fourteen) persons have been given current charge of the posts of Deputy Taxation Officer. 

 6. That the Writ Petitioner has got no experience in revenue works and as such it was not possible to consider his case to give him temporary charge of the post of Deputy Taxation officer. In para No. 2 of the said order it has been stated that temporary charge given to the persons shall not be treated as promotion and the person shall not raise any demand for promotion. That the said 14 persons have been promoted to the posts of Deputy Taxation Officer as stated in the Writ Petition is not correct. 

 9. The High Court Division made the rule absolute in part declaring the order of giving charge in the post of Deputy Taxation Officer so far it relates to Respondent Nos. 5 Mr. Md. Mainuddin, Assistant Social Welfare Officer, Respondent No. 12 Mr. Farid Ahmed, Marketing Supervisor, Respondent No. 13 Mr. Monjurul Haque, Marketing Supervisor, respondent No. 14 Mr. Mohsin Parvez Khan, Marketing Supervisor, respondent No. 15, Mr. Idris Ali, Marketing Supervisor, Respondent No. 16, Mr. Abu Md. Zahid Hassan, marketing Supervisor, Respondent No. 17 Mr. Rafiqul Islam, Marketing Supervisor and Respondent No. 18 Mr. Abdul Baaten Chowdhury, Marketing Supervisor are declared to have been made without any lawful authority and of no legal effect. The respondents are directed to take necessary action accordingly. 

 10. Mr. Abdur Razzaq, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the High Court Division ought to have held that the writ petition was premature in that by virtue of the Impugned Order the respondent Nos. 5 to 18 to the writ petition did not supersede the Writ petitioner inasmuch as the High Court Division has erred in law in holding that the impugned order was malafide without giving any finding as to who was liable for the malafide action, and failed to give any reason as to how he acted malafide and the High Court Division has committed error of law in holding that neither the post of Assistant Social Welfare Officer nor that of the Market Supervisor have been incorporated in the feeder post of D.T.O. and in that view of the matter they could not be given the current charge, inasmuch as to hold the current charge of a post one need not to hold the feeder post of that post. 

 11. The learned counsel further submits that the writ petitioner has got neither any experience to work in the Revenue Department nor he has ever been given any charge of revenue post rather the present petitioner being the Market Supervisors are performing Revenue activities and are eligible to be given current charge, of the posts of D.T.O. 

 12. It appears that the High Court Division arrived at a finding of fact that: 

 "On the face of the argument placed by the learned Advocates of both the sides and on perusal of the relevant provision of the Service Rule, 1989 and the impugned memo it is found that Respondent No. 5 Mr. Md. Mainuddin Appeal, Assistant Social Welfare Officer, Respondent No. 12, Mr. Farid Ahmed, Marketing Supervisor, respondent No. 13, Mr. Monjurul Haque, Marketing Supervisor, Respondent No. 14 Mr. Mohsin Parvez Khan. Marketing Supervisor, Respondent No. 15, Md. Idris Ali, Marketing Supervisor, Respondent No. 16, Mr. Abu Md. Zahid Hassan, Marketing Supervisor, Respondent No. 17 Mr. Rafiqul Islam, Marketing Supervisor and Respondent No. 18 Mr. Abdul Baten Chowdhury, Marketing Supervisor have been given in charge of the post Deputy Taxation Officer who are not, at all, qualified to be promoted in that post of D.T.O. and accordingly Respondent made a proposal to the Ministry in the 1993 under his office memo No. 286/f Exhx (pw-1) dated 15.08.1993 and reminders have been also issued to incorporate the designated Bazar Supervisor in the feeder post of the Deputy Taxation Officer given in schedule under Revenue Department but till now it has not been so received by the Corporation. This admitted facts certainly D.T.O. are completely product of malafide activities showing utter disregard to the Service Rule 1989 in order to provide some disqualified person in the higher post who are not, at all eligible to be promoted under Rule 16 of the Dhaka Municipal Corporation Employees Service Rule 1989." 

 "It is clear to us that neither Assistant Social Welfare officer nor Market Supervisor has yet been incorporated in the feeder post of D.T.O. under Dhaka Municipal Employee Service Rule 1989 so they are still disqualified and accordingly they cannot be posted to be in charge of the same. 

 13. It appears from record that previously on 17.12.94 a proposal was sent to the Secretary, Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operative for inclusion of the post of super for promotion to post of Deputy Taxation Officer but no sanction was given in spite of the remainder dated 26.11.93 Annexure-2 and 3 respectively and naturally the Corporation has designed a devise by giving charge to the post of Deputy Taxation Officer from amongst the persons who have been working in the proposed feeder post and possesses necessary experience for the purpose. The High Court Division while maintaining the order partially on scrutiny found certain appointee not to be qualified for holding charge temporarily.
